name: Austria: Vienna, Salzburg, Innsbruck, Hallstatt, the Wachau

destination.name: Austria: Vienna, Salzburg, Innsbruck, Hallstatt, the Wachau
destination.pitch: Vienna for coffee houses, Klimt and a 10 euro standing-room opera ticket, then west by Railjet: the Wachau's wine villages, Salzburg, Hallstatt after the day buses leave, and Innsbruck with a 2,637m ridge above the old town.

because.nature: The Nordkette lifts from central Innsbruck up under 2,637m, the Dachstein Five Fingers over a 400m drop, the glacier in Gosausee on a still morning, and 36km of Danube vineyard terraces by bike.
because.food: Tafelspitz at Plachutta, schnitzel at Figlmüller, a Melange and strudel at Café Sperl, a Bosna at Balkan Grill, Marillenknödel at the Kirchenwirt in Weissenkirchen, and the Knolls' lamb at Loibnerhof.
because.relaxation: Coffee houses built for two hours over one cup, the Donauinsel's swimmable channel, a Heuriger evening in Grinzing, and a slow boat from Krems to Melk.
because.culture: Klimt's The Kiss at the Upper Belvedere, the Schiele collection at the Leopold, Melk's library, Mozart's baptismal font in Salzburg Cathedral, and 1,200 painted skulls in Hallstatt's Beinhaus.
because.city: Vienna's Innere Stadt on foot, the Naschmarkt at 07:00, standing room at the opera, Loos's 1908 bar late; then Salzburg's Altstadt and Innsbruck's arcaded lanes as small, walkable second acts.

destination.caveat: The big sights queue hardest June to September and 10:00 to 16:00: book Schönbrunn online, walk Getreidegasse at 08:00, reach Hallstatt before 09:00. Café Central is shut for renovation through winter 2026, and fog closes the mountain lifts without notice. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Vienna
cities.base: The edge of the Innere Stadt by the Naschmarkt, on the 1st and 6th district border: walk to Stephansdom, the Hofburg and the opera, U4 to Schönbrunn, for less than the very centre.

cities.name: Salzburg
cities.base: The right-bank Altstadt around Linzergasse: quieter than Getreidegasse, a walk over the river to the cathedral and the fortress funicular, the Kapuzinerberg steps at your door.

cities.name: Innsbruck
cities.base: The Altstadt round the Golden Roof to walk everywhere, or Wilten by the basilica, cheaper and quieter, a short tram ride in.

cities.name: Hallstatt and the Salzkammergut
cities.base: Hallstatt itself if you book a lakeside guesthouse early, because you get the village after 17:00; otherwise Bad Ischl or Bad Goisern, cheaper, 15 to 20 minutes away.

cities.name: The Wachau
cities.base: Krems, the valley's biggest town, for beds, restaurants and the train to Vienna; Dürnstein if you want the blue tower outside your window and will pay for it.

places.name: Schönbrunn Palace
places.note: The Habsburgs' 1,441-room summer palace; the 49 euro Classic Pass covers the palace tour, gardens, maze and the Gloriette on the hill. Book a timed slot online, walk-up queues run 45 to 90 minutes in summer. The gardens open at 06:30 and are free.

places.name: Upper Belvedere
places.note: Prince Eugene's summer palace of 1714 to 1723, and you come for Klimt's The Kiss and the Austrian collection upstairs; the 1955 State Treaty was signed here. The Lower Belvedere across the garden does temporary shows.

places.name: St. Stephen's Cathedral
places.note: The Gothic cathedral begun in 1137 under 230,000 glazed roof tiles. The nave is free; the 343 steps up the 136m south tower and the catacombs are separate tickets. Mozart married here in 1782. Hours vary, check stephanskirche.at.

places.name: Hofburg Palace
places.note: The Habsburg city palace since the 13th century. The Sisi Museum, Imperial Apartments and Silver Collection share one ticket; the Augustinian Church next door, where Franz Joseph married Sisi, is free. Allow real walking time between wings. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Spanish Riding School
places.note: Lipizzaner stallions in the 1729 to 1735 Winter Riding Hall, the oldest classical dressage school, founded 1565. A morning training session is the cheap way in; a full performance needs booking well ahead. Hours vary, check srs.at.

places.name: Karlskirche
places.note: A plague-vow church built 1716 to 1737. The ticket includes a lift up into the dome, eye level with Rottmayr's fresco, which most visitors never see. Vivaldi concerts run here, and it is quieter than Stephansdom. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Naschmarkt
places.note: 1.5km of produce and food stalls along the Wienzeile since about 1820: weekdays to 21:00, Saturday to 18:00, closed Sunday. The Saturday flea market runs 06:30 to 14:00. Go early; it is picked over by noon and the lunch stalls queue.

places.name: Prater and the Riesenrad
places.note: Joseph II opened the park in 1766. The 1897 Giant Ferris Wheel, about 12 to 15 euros, is the ride worth paying for and turns all year; the Wurstelprater funfair is pay per ride and shuts November to mid-March. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Leopold Museum
places.note: The world's biggest Egon Schiele collection, plus Klimt and Kokoschka, in the old imperial stables. Closed Tuesdays. Stay for the free courtyards afterwards, where locals take the Enzis benches in the evening. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Albertina
places.note: About 65,000 drawings and a million old-master prints, Dürer among them, plus a strong Monet and Impressionist wing; over a million visitors in 2025. Albertina Modern, opened 2020, takes the 20th century. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Donauinsel
places.note: A 21km flood-control island built 1972 to 1988 that became the city's summer beach: a swimmable channel, a wakeboard lift, volleyball, naturist zones at both ends. Rent a bike at the Reichsbrücke end; you will see few tourists.

places.name: Vienna State Opera standing room
places.note: 567 standing places go on sale 80 minutes before curtain for 10 euros, cash, at the house, with 50 to 60 operas a year in repertory. The best-value night in Vienna if your legs last through act two. Hours vary, check the calendar.

places.name: Figlmüller Wollzeile
places.note: The schnitzel house since 1905; order the schnitzel, beaten out wider than the plate. Daily 11:00 to 22:30, kitchen to 21:30. Walk in at lunch; the dinner queue forms by 18:30.

places.name: Plachutta Wollzeile
places.note: The Tafelspitz house: boiled beef brought to the table in its copper pot, broth first, then the meat with apple-horseradish and chive sauce. Several cuts on the menu, so ask which. Daily 11:30 to 23:30.

places.name: Trzesniewski
places.note: Open-faced finger sandwiches, 26 kinds, eaten standing at the counter with a small Pfiff of beer; egg, herring and paprika cream cheese are the classics. 13 branches, the flagship on Dorotheergasse. Hours vary, check the branch.

places.name: Café Sperl
places.note: A coffee house since 1880 with its Thonet chairs, marble tables and billiard tables still in use; it is in Before Sunrise. Order a Melange and the apple strudel. Less overrun than Central or Sacher. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Zum Schwarzen Kameel
places.note: Here since 1618. Stand at the downstairs bar with a glass of wine, hand-cut ham and the small sandwiches; daily 08:00 to midnight, kitchen to 22:30, no booking. The restaurant upstairs takes reservations Tuesday to Saturday.

places.name: DECENTRAL, the Café Central pop-up
places.note: Café Central itself is shut for renovation from 16 March 2026 through the winter, so this pop-up two minutes away is where its kitchen went: pastries, focaccia, coffee and spritz, daily 07:30 to 22:00. Check whether the original has reopened.

places.name: Hengl-Haselbrunner, Grinzing
places.note: A working vineyard's Heuriger in Grinzing: a buffet, its own wine and live Heurigen music. Tuesday to Saturday from 15:30, closed Sunday and Monday; closing time not posted, hours vary, check. In the village, a pine branch over a door means that tavern is pouring.

places.name: Loos American Bar
places.note: Adolf Loos's 1908 bar, about 90 square feet made endless with mirrors and a marble ceiling; classic cocktails, daily noon to 04:00. Look for the small backlit onyx sign, it is easy to walk past, and no shorts or flip-flops.

places.name: Hohensalzburg Fortress
places.note: Begun in 1077, one of the largest surviving medieval castles in Europe. Ride the 1892 funicular up and book the combo online to skip the window queue. The 1502 Salzburg Bull organ plays daily Palm Sunday to 31 October. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Mirabell Palace Gardens
places.note: Gardens laid out from 1687, free and open about 06:30 to 20:00, with the Do-Re-Mi steps and the dwarf garden. The palace is city hall; only the Marble Hall opens, for concerts. Come before 09:00 for the fortress view without the groups.

places.name: Salzburg Cathedral
places.note: The Baroque rebuild of 1614 to 1628; Mozart was baptised in the font here in 1756 and it is still in use. The nave is free. The DomQuartier ticket next door adds the Residenz state rooms and museums, a good plan for rain. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Getreidegasse
places.note: The pedestrian lane of wrought-iron guild signs, McDonald's included. From 10:00 to 16:00 you see tour umbrellas, not ironwork; walk it at 08:00 or after 19:00.

places.name: Mozart's Birthplace
places.note: Mozart lived here until he was 17; a museum since 1880, with his childhood violin and family portraits. The rooms are small and bottleneck with groups, so go early, and buy the combo with his later family flat across the river. Open daily 9:00 to 17:30, last entry 30 minutes before close.

places.name: Mönchsberg lift and cliff walk
places.note: The lift has climbed the 508m ridge since 1890, to a free terrace over the roofs and the river; the Museum der Moderne at the top is a separate ticket. Walk the woods on top before heading down. Hours vary, check.

places.name: St. Peter's Abbey and Cemetery
places.note: A Benedictine abbey founded in 696. The arcaded cemetery and the catacomb chapels cut into the cliff are free to walk; the Sound of Music hiding scene was modelled on it. Quiet even when Getreidegasse, two minutes away, is jammed.

places.name: Hellbrunn Palace and trick fountains
places.note: An archbishop's day palace of 1613 to 1619 with no bedrooms, built for trick fountains: jets in a stone dining table soak you on the guided tour. There is one dry seat, the archbishop's. City bus from the centre. Open daily 9:30 to 18:30 in summer, shorter off season.

places.name: Untersberg cable car
places.note: An 8.5 minute ride up 1,320m to the summit plateau, with trails and a view over Salzburg and Berchtesgaden. Fog and wind stop it without notice; check the live status before the bus out and keep a fallback. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Kapuzinerberg
places.note: The 640m hill on the quiet bank, up the Imbergstiege steps from Linzergasse. The Basteiweg follows Thirty Years' War walls with old-town views and none of the Mönchsberg crowd; the friary on top dates from 1599.

places.name: St. Peter Stiftskulinarium
places.note: Named in a letter of 803 and claimed, not undisputed, as the oldest restaurant still running; you come for the room, not the cooking. Order the Salzburger Nockerl and look for a Mozart dinner-concert night. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Café Tomaselli
places.note: Family-run for over 150 years, and the Festival is said to have been dreamt up at its tables. Come for breakfast, which is the local habit: 07:00 to 19:00 Monday to Saturday, from 08:00 on Sundays.

places.name: Balkan Grill Walter
places.note: A window in a passage off Getreidegasse where the Bosna was invented in 1949: grilled pork sausage in white bread with onion, parsley and a secret spice mix. Daily 11:00 to 18:30, cash, no seats; eat it standing.

places.name: Sternbräu
places.note: Brewing on the site since 1542: a warren of halls and three beer gardens behind a plain Griesgasse door, easy for a group. Order the house Sternbier with a Wiener Schnitzel. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Fisch Krieg
places.note: A fishmonger with a stand-up bar on the Salzach embankment: a fried-fish roll or a herring sandwich eaten on your feet with the river in front of you. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Café Fürst, Alter Markt
places.note: Paul Fürst's own 1890 shop, still making the Mozartkugel to his 1915 recipe: pistachio marzipan, nougat, dark chocolate. Monday to Saturday 09:00 to 19:00, Sundays 10:00 to 17:00. Buy here, not the foil-wrapped supermarket brand.

places.name: Augustiner Bräustübl
places.note: The monastery beer hall in Mülln: about 900 seats inside and 1,500 under the chestnuts. Buy a stein at the counter, fill it, and get bread and radishes from the stalls. Weekdays from 15:00, weekends from 14:30, to 23:00. Cash, no cards.

places.name: Stiegl-Keller
places.note: Stiegl's terraced beer garden under the fortress, with what the house calls the best view over the Altstadt roofs, and the full Stiegl and Wildshut range. It seats 1,000 and can feel like an events hall; come for the view. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Golden Roof
places.note: 2,657 fire-gilded copper tiles over the royal box Maximilian I built for his wedding in 1500. Seeing it from the square is free and is the point; the small museum inside is skippable. The street jams at midday. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Nordkette via the Hungerburgbahn
places.note: Zaha Hadid's funicular to Hungerburg, then cable cars onto the ridge under the 2,637m Kleiner Solstein: high-alpine hiking 20 minutes from your hotel. Fog shuts the top section fast, so check before you buy. The Hafelekar summit lift runs about 9:00 to 18:00.

places.name: Alpenzoo
places.note: Alpine species only, and the highest zoo in Europe: bears, wolves, lynx and ibex with the city below. It has its own Hungerburgbahn stop, so fold it into the Nordkette day. Open daily 9:00 to 18:00 April to October, to 17:00 in winter.

places.name: Swarovski Kristallwelten
places.note: André Heller's crystal museum in Wattens, 17km east: 18 Chambers of Wonder, one with 800,000 hand-set crystals, on 7.5 hectares since 2015. The train and shuttle bus eat half a day; keep it for rain. Open daily 9:00 to 19:00, last entry 18:00.

places.name: Bergisel ski jump
places.note: Zaha Hadid's 2003 jump on the hill of the 1809 battles, still on the Four Hills Tournament. Take the lift to the top platform; the in-run looks far steeper than any photo. Open daily 9:00 to 18:00 June to October; shorter and closed Tuesdays the rest of the year.

places.name: Ambras Castle
places.note: Ferdinand II's Renaissance castle from 1563, with the only chamber of curiosities still in its original room and a 43m Spanish Hall of 27 portraits. Run by Vienna's Kunsthistorisches Museum. Bus, or 40 minutes on foot. Open daily 10:00 to 17:00, closed through November.

places.name: Hofkirche
places.note: Maximilian I's 1553 memorial, ringed by 28 bronze giants including a King Arthur designed by Dürer, though Maximilian is buried in Wiener Neustadt. Andreas Hofer's tomb and a 1560 organ are here too. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Wilten Basilica
places.note: A free Rococo pilgrimage basilica, far more lavish inside than a neighbourhood church should be, and off the Altstadt loop so nearly empty. Pair it with Bergisel, a short walk south.

places.name: Markthalle Innsbruck
places.note: Butchers, cheesemongers, a wine merchant and a few lunch counters on the Inn riverbank, where locals shop instead of the souvenir stalls. Monday to Saturday, closed Sunday; hours vary, check.

places.name: Hofburg Innsbruck
places.note: Maria Theresa's Rococo remodel with the Giant's Hall of family portraits; smaller and far quieter than the Vienna Hofburg. Two minutes from the Hofkirche, so do both together. Open daily 9:00 to 17:00, last admission 16:30.

places.name: Ottoburg
places.note: One of the oldest buildings in town, just below the Golden Roof, with wood-panelled Stuben: Gröstl, dumplings and game in season. Book the small upstairs rooms in summer. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Weisses Rössl
places.note: Three panelled rooms and a sun terrace with 600 years of innkeeping behind them; order the Alpine beef tartare. Lunch 11:30 to 14:00, dinner 17:30 to 21:30, closed Sundays and holidays. Locals eat here too.

places.name: Café Central Innsbruck
places.note: The self-styled most westerly Viennese coffee house, since 1884: 22 coffees, apple strudel and Guglhupf, jazz once a month. Daily 07:00 to 20:00. Unrelated to Vienna's Café Central.

places.name: Café Munding
places.note: Innsbruck's oldest café, 1803, in a room largely unchanged since 1936, with an 1809 cannonball still in the outside wall. Order cake, not lunch; it is a confectioner first. Open Tuesday to Saturday 9:00 to 18:00, closed Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Die Wilderin
places.note: Modern Tyrolean cooking from named Alpine farmers, 2 Gault Millau toques: the grey-cattle Tafelspitz or the roast duck. Tuesday to Sunday 17:00 to midnight, closed Mondays. A small room, so book.

places.name: Goldener Adler
places.note: An inn since 1390 where Goethe and Mozart both stayed, pouring regional drinks only. Order the Tyrolean char or the Gröstl. Daily 11:30 to 23:00, last orders 21:00, and the terrace is first come.

places.name: Batzenhäusl
places.note: A historic wood-panelled tavern in Igls, the Olympic bobsled village 5km south. Weekdays from 17:30, weekends from 14:00, kitchen to 22:00. A glass of wine after an afternoon up the Patscherkofel side.

places.name: Hallstatt village and lakefront
places.note: 778 people on a strip between the lake and the Dachstein, UNESCO since 1997, and up to 30,000 day visitors on a peak day. Walk the lakefront and the square before 09:00 or after 17:00 and it is a different place.

places.name: Salzwelten salt mine and Skywalk
places.note: The oldest salt mine still worked, 7,000 years of it: funicular up, mine train, miners' slides and an underground salt lake, with the Skywalk 360m over the village. Parking is scarce, take the bus. Open daily 9:30 to 16:30, shorter from late October.

places.name: Beinhaus, St. Michael's Chapel
places.note: Over 1,200 skulls, many painted with names, dates and flowers, stacked because the churchyard ran out of room. Small, quiet, and more unsettling than the lake photos prepare you for. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Hallstatt World Heritage Museum
places.note: Bronze and Iron Age finds from the mine that named a European period, 800 to 450 BC, including some of the best-kept prehistoric textiles in Europe. Small; pair it with the Beinhaus. Open daily 10:00 to 18:00 May to September, shorter and later-opening off season.

places.name: Dachstein Krippenstein and Five Fingers
places.note: Cable car from Obertraun onto the Dachstein to the Five Fingers platform over a 400m drop, with the Mammut and Giant Ice caves. The glaciers here are retreating fast. Weather decides the day; check first. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Vorderer Gosausee
places.note: The Dachstein glacier reflected in the lake on a still morning, with a fraction of Hallstatt's crowd. A flat lakeside path anyone can walk; drive, or take the Gosau bus from Bad Ischl, and go early.

places.name: Kaiservilla, Bad Ischl
places.note: Franz Joseph's summer house for decades, where he signed the declaration of war on Serbia on 28 July 1914. The family still owns part of it, so only sections open. Follow it with cake at Zauner. Open daily 9:30 to 17:00 May to September; shorter shoulder-season hours.

places.name: Schafbergbahn, St. Wolfgang
places.note: A rack railway up the Schafberg above the Wolfgangsee, one of the last of its kind in the Alps. The 1481 Pacher altarpiece in St. Wolfgang's church is worth the stop even without the train. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Bräugasthof
places.note: Family-run since 1504, home cooking from local produce. Skip the photo menu out front and order the day's schnitzel or goulash. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Gasthof Zauner
places.note: On the market square: lake trout and regional plates, and a terrace that fills first when a tour bus lands, so eat after 17:00. No relation to Café Zauner in Bad Ischl. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Restaurant im Kainz
places.note: The one dinner a notch above the Gasthof standard, billed by the town as a meeting place for gourmets. Hours vary, check, and confirm the menu before you book the evening.

places.name: Café Zauner, Bad Ischl
places.note: Pastry in Franz Joseph's summer capital since 1832, about 250 cakes and 60 chocolates. Buy a Zaunerstollen, the nougat and marzipan bar, to take home. Daily 08:30 to 18:00.

places.name: Rudolfsturm
places.note: A 13th-century tower at the top of the salt-mine funicular with a terrace over the lake; the best lunch view in the area, worth the fare even without the mine. Cakes as well as meals. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Weisses Rössl, St. Wolfgang
places.note: The real inn behind the operetta The White Horse Inn, with a terrace on the Wolfgangsee. Lunch here on the Schafbergbahn day. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Simple 169
places.note: A small place on the lake road with house-made food, lower-key than the square: a drink and a light bite once the day buses leave. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Zum Bader
places.note: The quiet room the town directory calls its romantic option, for a glass of Austrian wine after 17:00 when the crowd has gone. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Salzberg trail to the mine overlook
places.note: The footpath to the salt mine climbs the back lanes and switchbacks to the classic high view of the lake, for free. Steep, 40 to 60 minutes; turn back before the mine gate if the view is all you want.

places.name: Echern Valley and Waldbachstrub
places.note: A valley walk behind the village to the Waldbachstrub waterfall, one of the routes up to the Dachstein; almost nobody on it, 15 minutes from the square. Confirm the trailhead signs locally.

places.name: Melk Abbey
places.note: A Benedictine abbey since 1089 in a Baroque shell of 1702 to 1736; 16 euros covers the church, the library and the museum. April to October 09:00 to 17:30, last entry 17:00. Skip the 4 euro guided surcharge; self-guided covers it.

places.name: Dürnstein castle ruins
places.note: Where Leopold V held Richard the Lionheart in 1192; wrecked by the Swedes in 1645, now a free, unguarded ruin. 30 to 40 minutes up an unpaved path to the best view of the Danube bend. Wear proper shoes.

places.name: Dürnstein Abbey
places.note: The Augustinian abbey whose powder-blue tower is the most photographed building in the Wachau. A quick visit inside; the best angle is from the riverside promenade or the castle path. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Göttweig Abbey
places.note: Founded 1083 and still home to about 30 monks; the largest Baroque staircase in Austria climbs to Troger's 1739 fresco. Buy the abbey's own apricot jam in the shop. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Krems Altstadt and Steiner Tor
places.note: The 1480 Steiner Tor and a medieval core that once nearly matched Vienna in size; now the valley's wine-trade town and home of Marillenschnaps. Walk it before dinner in Stein.

places.name: Kunsthalle Krems
places.note: Modern and contemporary shows on the Kunstmeile, next to the caricature museum; the antidote after two days of Baroque abbeys. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Domäne Wachau
places.note: The valley's big cooperative, good Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at every ripeness from Steinfeder to Smaragd. Tasting room weekdays 10:00 to 17:00, Saturday to 14:00 April to October, closed Sunday. The Heuriger tent runs a few days in July.

places.name: DDSG boat, Krems to Melk
places.note: Up to four sailings a day each way from May to early October, 2.5 to 3 hours, about 37 euros one way and 44 return. Bikes ride along for 3 euros, so pair it with the cycle path. Hours vary, check the timetable.

places.name: Danube cycle path
places.note: About 36km of flat, paved path past every terrace and abbey in the valley. Rent in Krems, ride to Melk, and put the bike on the boat back rather than ride home into the afternoon headwind.

places.name: Spitz and the Tausendeimerberg
places.note: A cobbled wine town under the Tausendeimerberg, the hill said to have filled a thousand buckets in one harvest. A stop on the bike path rather than a destination, with a couple of Heurigen for a break.

places.name: Schallaburg
places.note: A Renaissance castle with an arcaded courtyard 5km from Melk, hosting one big changing exhibition rather than a permanent collection. Check what is on before the detour. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Loibnerhof
places.note: The Knoll family's restaurant, serious wine-country cooking: the herb-crusted lamb and the goose liver pâté. Wednesday to Saturday 11:30 to 23:00, kitchen to 19:00; Sunday to 21:30. Closed Monday and Tuesday; book weekends.

places.name: Restaurant Jamek
places.note: A working estate's Michelin-listed restaurant. Lunch 11:30 to 16:00 Tuesday to Thursday and Saturday, dinner too on Friday 17:30 to 23:00; closed Sunday and Monday. Drink the Ried Achleiten Grüner Veltliner.

places.name: Melk Abbey restaurant
places.note: The abbey's own restaurant at the visitor entrance: convenient rather than special, and useful for lunch between the abbey and the boat dock 10 minutes below. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Kirchenwirt Weissenkirchen
places.note: Vaulted rooms, a vine-arbour terrace and a garden under a century-old linden. Order the Marillenknödel, apricot dumplings made in the house. Daily 11:00 to 19:30 until 1 November 2026, shorter after that.

places.name: Wachauerstube Loiben
places.note: A country inn cooking above its station: trout with wasabi, rice pudding with pumpkin and apricot, a strong wine list. Monday, Saturday and Sunday 11:30 to 20:00, Friday dinner 17:00 to 22:00, closed Tuesday to Thursday.

places.name: Salzstadl
places.note: A riverfront pub and stage in Stein with regional cooking and a live Bühne frei programme. 11:00 to 15:00 and 18:00 to 23:00, Tuesday lunch only, closed Wednesday and Sunday. Check what is on if the music is the point.

places.name: Jamek wine shop
places.note: Taste and buy at the estate without the lunch booking: Monday to Friday 09:00 to 16:00, Sunday 10:00 to 15:00, closed Saturday. Ask for the 2025 Jochinger Riesling Federspiel.
